targets.authors: Schatzschneider C Bruder G Steinicke F
targets.title: Who turned the clock? Effects of manipulated zeitgebers, cognitive load and immersion on time estimation
targets.evidence_quote: To establish the robustness of the sun-speed effect reported by Schatzschneider et al. 28 , we attempted a conceptual replication 29 .
targets.outcome_quote: We did not replicate the original effect, as reported by Schatzschneider et al., however, we did find that the perceived duration of an interval was affected by cognitive load, fatigue, and unpleasant symptoms caused by VR.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly state nonreplication of the central sun-speed effect and also report no overall immersion effect. Cognitive load confirms a classical background effect and the other new findings do not change the verdict about the targeted sun-speed effect.

reasoning: New participants and a reconstructed VR environment re-test Schatzschneider et al. (2016). Other citations provide background, a task, or methodological context; the cognitive-load meta-analysis is not an independent original empirical target.
